gaps.sentence: 'The flight leaves now,' the announcer said. The announcer said that the flight left ___.
gaps.explanation: Now becomes then in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'You must be joking!' I exclaimed. I exclaimed that he ___ be joking.
gaps.hint: must of deduction does not backshift
gaps.explanation: Must expressing confident deduction usually stays must; only obligation shifts to had to.

gaps.sentence: 'Which seat do you prefer?' the steward asked. The steward asked which seat I ___.
gaps.explanation: do you prefer → I preferred: statement order, present simple backshifted.

gaps.sentence: 'I'm exhausted,' she said. She said she ___ exhausted.
gaps.explanation: Present simple/progressive shifts to past in reported speech: am → was.

gaps.sentence: 'Don't forget to lock up,' my mother said. My mother reminded me ___ up.
gaps.explanation: 'Don't forget' corresponds to remind + object + to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'I saw him this morning,' she said on Monday afternoon. She said she had seen him ___ morning.
gaps.explanation: This morning, reported later the same day, becomes that morning.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll carry those bags for you,' he said. He ___ to carry my bags.
gaps.explanation: Offers of help are reported as offered to do something.

gaps.sentence: 'Would you like to stay for dinner?' they asked. They ___ me to stay for dinner.
gaps.explanation: Offers of this kind are reported as invited somebody to do something.
